This frame is used when the client is in a competitive market and he has to pivot to a evolving market, rather than compete in the same market. This is built on the hypothesis that all markets evolve in multiple directions and saturated markets slowly loose customers to these evolving markets. Players in the market should be pioneers in the market to capture this market before the rest come for the market. Large players, who have the bandwidh to invest in resources are advised to stay in well established markets as they have a large customer base. These players can actively invest in writing more blogs, covering AEO, slowly pivot to SEO based content, do outreach programs, gain reviews, get PR placements. This frame is when small players can't compete with these large players by investing so many reviews and will have to find niche markets in a category. Categories evolve in multiple directions like industry specialization , use case focused, technology advancement, regional players, operational efficiency, cost, size specific, ....

I don't think we will need a vertical category evolution framework because that is not something that is marketing-related or marketing-intensive. It is basically something the client does with selling more products to the same customer. That's the reason why we don't have a vertical category evolution frame, only a horizontal category evolution frame.

Write ICPs as trapped-demand descriptions, not company profiles. Each one is a single prose paragraph describing a buyer's stuck position, containing: what they already believe without my telling them; what they already want as a result; proof that money is not the constraint (ideally money already spent and wasted); evidence they are actively searching right now; and the specific structural blocker that would survive them writing a large cheque tomorrow.
